subject: Sandpit vs Hosted vs VPC — Trial scope, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@carelyft.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Trial environment options & success metrics

Hi Kimberly / Marissa (and Ben),

Thanks for a helpful call today — good to knock through the high-level use case. To make sure we scope the POC correctly, a few clarifying items from our side and a request for your recommended path: hosted API vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC/private deployment. Summary: we want to validate retrieval-augmented generation for our care planning assistant with patient-facing summaries. Key constraints: PHI in input (must be redacted in logs), US-only data residency, and predictable 95th percentile latency under load.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm the difference in setup effort and timeline for hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial? (how long to get us running with our sample data)
- Do you have a recommended default for teams with PHI + moderate throughput (expected 8–12 qps peak)?
- Suggested success criteria we should include in the MOU (latency targets, throughput, cost estimate, quality checks).
- Security checklist owners — we’ll need SOC 2 artifacts and an infra/network diagram for our security team.

We can provide a sanitized subset of our dataset (5000 anonymized notes) next week. Proposed kickoff window: Apr 12–15.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Director of AI Platforms, Carelyft

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Trial environment options & success metrics

Amit — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a proposed, pragmatic plan (short + actionable) so we can finalize scope and owners ahead of kickoff. I’ve attached a spreadsheet with concrete success criteria (trial_success_criteria.xlsx) and our standard network doc (carelyft_network_requirements.pdf).

Proposed trial options (high level):
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted API; minimal setup (API keys, sample dataset upload to a secure ingestion endpoint). Timeline: ~48–72 hours to validate generator + RAG on a small corpus. Data controls: request-level logging by default; we can enable no-persist with a request flag for PII-sensitive calls. Good fit if you want quick signal and low ops overhead.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU capacity in our shared infra with isolation and predictable throughput. Timeline: ~5–7 business days for resource allocation + config. Good for longer-running load tests and realistic throughput gating.
- VPC / Private (most secure): Private control plane + customer VPC peering or on-prem package. Timeline: typically 2–3 weeks (security review, network setup, KMS integration). Best for PHI with strict egress/data residency requirements.

Suggested success criteria (summary — full table in attached spreadsheet):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for single-turn generation (goal); <= 400ms acceptable for RAG with external vector store calls.
- Throughput: sustain 10 qps for 15 minutes with <5% error rate.
- Quality: ROUGE/ROUGE-L and human eval on 200-case sample with target F1 thresholds (see sheet).
- Security: SOC 2 Type II evidence, automated deletion of test logs on request, encryption-at-rest using your KMS (if VPC).
- Data handling: no model-fine-tuning with PHI; all training traces disabled for hosted unless explicitly agreed.

Owners / roles:
- Redwood AE/owner: Kimberly Park (me) — commercial / timeline owner
- Trial ops & onboarding: Marissa Cole — MOU + environment provisioning
- Solutions / infra: Ben Carter — model selection, batching, perf tuning
- Private deployment & networking: Rishi Malhotra — VPC/KMS/network coordination
- Carelyft point: Amit Shah / Samantha Lee — dataset, security PO, success signoff

Immediate next steps (we recommend):
1) Confirm desired environment (hosted / dedicated / VPC). If you want to start fast, we suggest Hosted for initial quality + functional validation, then move to Dedicated or VPC for scale and PHI controls.
2) Share the sanitized sample dataset (aim for the 5k notes you mentioned) and a single example of the expected prompt/response pattern.
3) Security: please send your standard questionnaire to security@redwood.com (cc me + Marissa). We will attach SOC 2 artifacts and an infra diagram within 48 hours of receipt.
4) Tentative kickoff: Wed Apr 14 at 10am PT — we’ll hold a 45-minute technical kickoff with owners above.

If that works, I’ll draft a short MOU (one page) summarizing success criteria, timeline and owners for signatures.

Thanks — Kim

> Suggested success criteria (summary — full table in attached spreadsheet):
> - Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for single-turn generation (goal); <= 400ms acceptable for RAG with external vector store calls.
> - Throughput: sustain 10 qps for 15 minutes with <5% error rate.

Quick technical notes / clarifications from my side:
- For RAG workloads the external vector DB (we use an example config in the spreadsheet) will add variable tail latency — in Hosted we recommend keeping vector lookups batched and using our KV cache for repeated queries to hit the latency targets.
- Model/quantization: for the hosted POC we propose using the 7B quantized variant to get a good cost/latency tradeoff; if you need exact parity with your production model we can pin a larger model in Dedicated or VPC.
- Dataset: 5k notes is fine for a baseline. Please include a 200-case labeled evaluation set (we’ll use this for human eval + automated metrics).
- Ports / networking: if you go VPC, Rishi will need an IP allowlist and a short windows for SSH/peering to verify. See the network doc attached.

I’ll own the perf tuning during the trial and plan a focused perf run on day 5 of the POC if we go Dedicated.

—Ben

1) Phase 1 (Week 1): Hosted POC for quality/functional validation. Carelyft will provide the 5k anonymized notes + 200 labeled cases by Apr 9. Redwood to spin up hosted keys and a small sandbox test within 72 hours.
2) Phase 2 (Week 2–3): If Phase 1 meets quality criteria, move to Dedicated sandbox for sustained throughput tests and perf tuning (Ben to run day-5 perf run).
3) Phase 3 (if needed): VPC/private deployment (we’ll start security review in parallel if Phase 2 shows promise).

Kickoff: Apr 14 at 10am PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite with the tech agenda. Also:
- We’ll circulate our security questionnaire to security@redwood.com by EOD Apr 6.
